A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLBS research. Their main text, mathematical content, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original video and image generation experiments, reward-calibration analyses, and VLM and human evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds fine-tuning, reward-transfer, gradient-method, and longer-video experiments.

M1.justification: DLBS beam selection, deterministic lookahead estimation, reward calibration, and Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged. Applying the existing procedure to fine-tuned models or a VideoScore reward constitutes additional experimental configurations, rather than a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The existing datasets and basic video/image generation tasks are retained. Appendix J.4 adds an explicit cross-dataset transfer scenario: rewards calibrated on DEVIL-high or DEVIL-medium are applied to MSRVTT-test, extending evaluation beyond calibration matched to the target prompt set.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated VideoDPO and gradient-based DAS comparisons. Its main human evaluation also adds BoN with KB=64 as a comparator; the earlier comparison against GS with KB=1 remains in Appendix M.11. FK Steering was already evaluated in v2 and is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include human comparisons at 2500 versus 3200 NFE, 49-/81-frame generation, Stable Diffusion 1.5/DAS comparisons, and direct VideoScore-reward search. Separately, the reference DDIM rollout in the estimation-error diagnostic changes from eta=0 in v2 Figure 21 to eta=1 in v3 Figure 23; whether this reflects a correction or rerun is unstated.

E4.justification: v3 adds reward-transfer analysis, examination of the top 5% VLM–human disagreement cases, and lookahead ablations using SDE-DPMSolver++ on Wan 2.1. Longer-video and fine-tuning compatibility tests further examine applicability. The diversity analysis, including its plotted DLBS-LA results, already existed in v2 and is largely relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pearson-correlation significance and reward averages across prompts. v3 introduces no new repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 add fine-tuning, calibration-cost, transfer, direct-VideoScore, resource-comparison, and maximum-frame results. For example, Table 1 reports DPO+DLBS scores of 0.359/0.576 versus DPO's 0.335/0.556 on DEVIL-high/MSRVTT-test. New human-comparison and cross-sampler results are also reported. The revised DDIM error curve has a different stated reference condition, preventing a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: The stochastic-control derivation and lookahead convergence/Lipschitz argument are unchanged; v2 Appendix E becomes v3 Appendix F. The diversity definition, Equation 15, moves from Appendix L.7 to Appendix D without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the compute-allocation recommendation: v2 prioritizes lookahead steps over search budget or denoising steps, whereas v3 recommends enabling lookahead and increasing search budget before expanding denoising steps. The central calibration, parameter-update-free alignment, and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning cross-dataset reward transfer, complementarity with VideoDPO, and the memory limitations of gradient-based search. Appendix K discusses VLM failures involving text, quantities, and anatomy. Section 7 replaces the proposed extension to human feedback with a recommendation for more specialized evaluators, including physical-law assessment.

D1.justification: v3 adds hardware, reward, budget, and frame-duration information for new comparisons, but removes Section 5's explicit min/max reward-normalization statement. Appendix B switches its code pointer to GitHub, which was already listed in v2's front matter; this does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: v3 adds the VideoDPO citation and positions DLBS as complementary to fine-tuning, while expanding discussion of resource tradeoffs with the already-cited DAS method. The remaining cited works and overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v3 edits grammar and terminology, promotes diversity analysis into Section 5.4, adds a fine-tuning subsection, and separates diversity details into Appendix D. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact; the publication footer and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: v3 introduces eight tables, expands Figure 2 with additional model examples, and adds failure-case and cross-sampler figures. It reorganizes human/diversity panels, expands the main-text VideoScore display using existing appendix results, and revises the lookahead-error plot's axes and curves. Many other plots are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new human comparison against higher-budget BoN provides a stronger control than v2's main no-search comparison, while transfer, longer-video, and DAS tests strengthen empirical support. These benefits outweigh a localized reporting defect: new Table 2 assigns approximately 102,400 seconds to 1600 queries at 15 seconds each, although those assumptions imply 24,000 seconds, overstating the estimated cost advantage.
